correctness.rationale: The first-step projected equations give y_G=1/(2a), y_MR=a/(2a²+b²), y_PMR=a/[2(a²+b²)]. Direct residual expansion shows squared norm (1−2ay)²+2b²y² and strict residual order for b>0. The exact positive Gramian has vᵀXv=∫(vᵀe^(−Ht)v)²dt>1/(2a) by strict spectral Jensen when b>0; the quadratic Frobenius error then decreases throughout the interval containing y_PMR<y_MR<y_G. Exact rational 2×2 matrices give squared Galerkin error asymptotic 3/(4K²), PMR error tending to 1/16, and residual PMR/G ratio tending to sqrt(3)/2. Equality b=0 is proved. Embedded standard-library verifier replay passed 3695 deterministic exact-rational assertions; no finite tests substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The natural stopping/selection question for low-rank Lyapunov solvers is whether smaller computable Frobenius residual means smaller true matrix-solution error. The theorem answers this negatively for *every* non-eigenvector first-step symmetric rank-one case and quantifies a diverging PMR/Galerkin error ratio despite constant-factor residual improvement. This is a structurally motivated benchmark for residual-vs-error reliability, not arbitrary parameter slicing or a mere routine normalization check; it makes no claim about multi-step superiority.
